tools.input: const patch = "*** Begin Patch *** Add File: /app/agent-output/S19-phantom-update-stale-host/report.md +# S19 — Phantom update, stale host half, and corrupted payload + +## Conclusion + +The evidence shows three independent boundaries, not one bad release artifact: + +1. The v0.3.7 client bundle was built while the manifest still said `0.3.6`, so + it permanently contains `PLUGIN_VERSION = "0.3.6"`. The update check compares + that baked value with the mirror tag and consequently treats `v0.3.7` as newer. +2. The browser obtained the refreshed client bundle, but the host process was not + restarted. Its in-memory asset-route registration still had the old extension + whitelist, even though the installed `lib/index.js` on disk already contains + the SVG entry. +3. The disk SVG is valid. The malformed value is the text assembled and persisted + as the session result. The plugin must therefore reject that result as an + untrusted rendering input and report the upstream result-text corruption. + +## 1. Phantom self-update + +The version used by the self-update check is a build-time value. The shipped +`lib/client.js` says: + +```js +export const PLUGIN_VERSION = "0.3.6"; +``` + +The bundle excerpt also states that tsdown inlined this value from `package.json` +when the bundle was built; the running client does not read the manifest at +runtime. The release log gives the causality: + +```text +16:22 build +16:23 package.json 0.3.6 -> 0.3.7 +``` + +Thus the operation-order mistake was bumping the manifest after generating the +artifact. The subsequent commit and tag included that already-built stale +`lib/client.js`. The tag and all three mirrors were consistent with one another, +but they consistently delivered an artifact whose embedded version was wrong. + +At the v0.3.7 symptom point, the mirror's `v0.3.7` tag is greater than the +bundle's `0.3.6`, so `compareSemver("v0.3.7", PLUGIN_VERSION) > 0` returns true +and the badge says `新版本 v0.3.7 可用`. The later evidence listing also shows +that the v0.3.7 and v0.3.8 tag SHAs are identical across `origin`, `public`, and +`omdsh`; that verifies mirror/tag integrity, not the semantic correctness of a +generated constant. + +The safe release order is: + +1. Make the source change and tests. +2. Bump the manifest to the target version **before** building, and update any + release references. +3. Build and test the generated artifacts. +4. Inspect the artifact before pushing. For v0.3.7, a check such as + `rg -n 'PLUGIN_VERSION|0\.3\.6|0\.3\.7' lib/client.js` must show the target + value (`"0.3.7"`) and must not show the old baked value in the version + constant. More robustly, a release check should extract the shipped constant + and compare it with the manifest version. +5. Commit source, manifest, and generated files together; tag that commit; then + verify the tag object/commit SHA independently on every mirror. + +That shipped-bundle check would have caught the phantom update before any push. +The mirror SHA check remains valuable, but it is a distribution-integrity check, +not a build-content check. + +## 2. Client plane versus host plane + +The two halves have different lifecycles: + +| Plane | Evidence/code | Load point | Effect of the v0.3.8 update | +|---|---|---|---| +| Client | shipped `lib/client.js`, including the render toggle | The plugin frontend fetches/reloads the client bundle in the browser | The browser refreshed, so the new toggle appeared and was clickable | +| Host | `lib/index.js`, including `CONTENT_TYPES` and the asset route registration | The running host loads the host module at boot and keeps the route handler/whitelist in memory | No host restart occurred, so the old route behavior remained active | + +The probes isolate the failure to the running host process. The PNG request gets +`200 image/png`, proving that the route is registered and alive. The SVG request +gets the route's `404 "unsupported image type"`, which is an extension-whitelist +decision rather than a missing route. At the same time, the disk copy of the +v0.3.8 `lib/index.js` contains `svg: 'image/svg+xml'`. Therefore the file on disk +and the code in the release are ahead of the code already loaded by the host. + +A host-plane change becomes effective only after the host process is restarted, +or after an explicit host/plugin reload mechanism that unloads the old module and +runs route registration again. A client hot refresh changes browser code; it does +not mutate JavaScript objects, route tables, or module state in a separately +running host. This is the exception to the usual “plugins hot-update” expectation: +that rule covers the client plane here, while route registration is boot-time host +state and needs a host restart/reload. + +## 3. Broken-image attribution + +The source and payload disagree in a directly testable way. The source's line 232 +ends with a normal `stroke-width="6.5"`; the stored payload has that line ending +in the partial attribute text `stro`, followed by line 247's arc tail beginning +`0,1 821,730`. The real source lines 233–247 are absent. This produces the parser +error at the corrupted `stro0` attribute. The source passes `System.Xml` +well-formedness, and a later read is clean. + +The corruption therefore occurred while the read-result text was being assembled +and persisted in the session-log/result layer upstream of the plugin. It did not +occur in the SVG file, in the host asset route, or in the plugin's renderer. The +read tool's separate TYPE result being clean is consistent with a corruption of +the model-visible text block rather than the underlying file-read operation. + +The plugin must treat session result text as untrusted input: a successful tool +call or a clean type field is not proof that the returned text is intact. It must +validate the SVG before creating a render source and surface the validation error +with enough context to diagnose the result pipeline. + +Editing or “repairing” the traced file would have been the wrong response. The +file on disk is already well-formed, and the missing source lines cannot be safely +recovered by modifying the canonical asset based on a corrupted observation. +That would risk damaging good user data and would conceal the upstream +non-deterministic text-corruption bug. The correct action is to use a clean +source/read and report the result-text assembly defect upstream. + +## 4. Defensive SVG render chain + +Use the following ordered sources. A failed level should fall through with a +diagnostic reason; it should not leave a broken `` as the apparent result. + +1. **Disk-bytes asset route.** Request the host asset route for the original path + and, on a successful response with the expected SVG content type, render the + response bytes (for example through a Blob/object URL). This is canonical, + avoids a text round-trip through the session log, preserves the exact file, + and allows the host to apply its path and content-type policy. In this + incident it will fail until the stale host is restarted, which is an expected + diagnosable fallback condition. +2. **Validated session payload.** Only if the route is unavailable, and only if a + session payload is present, parse it as SVG XML before rendering it. In a + browser this can be: + + ```js + const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(payload, "image/svg+xml"); + const invalid = doc.querySelector("parsererror"); + if (invalid || doc.documentElement?.localName !== "svg") { + throw new Error("session SVG is not well-formed"); + } + ``` + + The exact DOMParser error handling should also account for the target browser, + but the essential gate is rejecting a `parsererror` (and a non-`svg` root). + Only the validated text/bytes may then be used for an image/object URL. The + incident payload fails this gate at `stro0`, so it must not be handed to the + image decoder. +3. **Sandboxed iframe as the last render fallback.** For a valid SVG that cannot + be displayed through the normal image path, load it in an iframe with a + restrictive sandbox, such as `sandbox=""`, without `allow-scripts` or + `allow-same-origin` (and apply an appropriate restrictive CSP). The sandbox + blocks SVG script execution while declarative SMIL animations can still run. + This gives animated SVGs a document context without granting the untrusted + document the plugin page's script or origin privileges. A malformed session + payload does not bypass the XML gate merely because an iframe is available. +4. **Explicit error state.** If the asset route fails, the payload is absent or + fails XML validation, and no safe fallback renders, show a deliberate error + state such as “SVG preview unavailable: asset route unavailable and session + payload is malformed,” with retry/re-read diagnostics. Remove or replace the + broken image element so the user is not given a silent generic broken-image + icon. + +The order prioritizes the authoritative byte source, permits the session source +only when its syntax proves intact, limits the capabilities of the document-level +fallback, and makes data loss visible instead of silently displaying corrupted +content. + +## 5. Forensics and prevention + +### Decoding the concatenated-Zstandard log + +The raw generation file should be copied to a separate temporary working path and +hashed first; the evidence directory remains read-only. Decode it as a sequence of +Zstandard frames, preserving bytes and boundaries: + +1. Open the file in binary mode and initialize a Zstandard streaming decompressor. + A frame starts with the Zstandard magic bytes `28 b5 2f fd`, but magic-byte + searching alone must not be used to split frames because those bytes can occur + inside compressed data. +2. Give the decoder the remaining input and retain both its output bytes and the + input position it reports as consumed. Continue until it reports end-of-frame + (`ret == 0` in the libzstd streaming API). Record the input offset/length, + output offset/length, and hashes for that frame. +3. Advance by the decoder-reported consumed count and repeat for the next frame + until EOF. If using a language binding, use its one-frame/`unused_data` or + `bytes_consumed` facility; do not rely only on a CLI invocation that silently + concatenates all decompressed output and loses frame provenance. +4. Concatenate the decompressed bytes in frame order, then parse the resulting + log records. Preserve UTF-8 bytes, line endings, and whitespace while extracting + the read-result text. Save the raw frame map and hashes alongside the decoded + excerpt so another investigator can reproduce the exact stored value. +5. Compare the stored result with an independent fresh read only as an attribution + check. Do not fill missing lines from that fresh read when reporting what the + session log actually stored. In this case the exact stored payload includes the + `stro` + line-247-tail splice and is not well-formed XML; the clean re-read is + separate evidence that the source was not damaged. + +The fixture provides the decoded excerpt, not the raw generation file, so the +procedure above is the reproducible frame-level method for the underlying artifact +rather than a mutation of the evidence pack. + +### Checklist additions + +- Bump the version before building; make the manifest, source, and generated + artifacts part of the same reviewable change. +- Grep or programmatically inspect the shipped bundle for the baked version and + fail the release if it differs from the manifest/tag target. +- Verify the tag's commit/object SHA on every mirror, retaining the per-mirror + evidence. Keep this as a distribution check in addition to the bundle-content + check. +- After host-plane changes, record a host restart/reload and probe a changed route + or content type from the running process; a client refresh alone is insufficient. +- Treat session-log read-result text as untrusted: perform XML well-formedness + validation before SVG rendering and retain the original failure diagnostics. +- Report the upstream session/result-text corruption bug with the exact frame, + offsets/record, malformed splice, and clean re-read comparison. Do not paper it + over by editing or “repairing” a valid traced file in the plugin. + *** End Patch"; text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));
